picks.title: Elsevier Launches AI Assistant for Healthcare E-books
picks.excerpt: Elsevier's Nora AI lets healthcare students ask questions about their course materials and get answers without leaving the e-book. The assistant is scoped to the publisher's own licensed content rather than the open web.
picks.rationale: A major educational publisher shipping an in-book assistant scoped to licensed content turns the e-book from a container into an interface — the clearest new brief for reading-product designers.

picks.title: Calibre ebook manager lets you generate AI book covers in a click
picks.excerpt: Calibre 9.14 adds generative AI cover creation to the open-source e-book manager, letting users produce and swap in a cover image from a prompt inside the library tool itself.
picks.rationale: Cover generation shipping as a default feature in mainstream reader software lands directly on book-cover design work and on what readers now expect a jacket to be.

picks.title: AI vs. Human Audiobook Narration: A Blinded Survey of 1,000 Listeners
picks.excerpt: A blinded listening study of 1,000 audiobook consumers testing whether people can tell AI narration from human narration — and whether knowing changes how much they say they'd pay.
picks.rationale: Actual listener data instead of vibes on synthetic narration — the number publishers and narrators will both cite in the next contract fight.

picks.title: “A Secure Environment to Explore”: The AI Sandbox Initiative For Staff at the Library of Congress
picks.excerpt: The Library of Congress has stood up an internal AI sandbox so staff can test generative tools against collections work in a controlled environment before anything touches public services.
picks.rationale: A rare, concrete rollout model — sandbox first, workflow second — that any content or collections organization can copy tomorrow.

picks.title: Recognizing ‘Human’ Contributions, Longlist Revealed for the 26th getAbstract International Book Award
picks.excerpt: The 2026 getAbstract award longlist is explicitly framed around recognizing human authorship and contribution, with winners to be announced October 8 at the Frankfurt Book Fair.
picks.rationale: Prizes are starting to certify “human-made” as a category — an early signal of how authorship credit gets defined and marketed in an AI-saturated list.
